proof.text: First check the hypotheses of the completion and open-extension results. The finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes all four schemes Noetherian. The locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness lemma makes them qcqs. Every inverse image of $U$ in an affine open of $X$ is a Noetherian open subscheme and therefore quasi-compact; thus $j$ is quasi-compact, and the same argument applies to $j'$. The coefficient theorem makes $R$ a principal ideal domain with finite residue field. Every ideal is generated by one element, so $R$ is Noetherian. Each $A_n$ is finite by the finite-quotient theorem, and $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ is a finite free resolution of $A_n$, since $t$ is nonzero in the domain $R$. Thus $(R,(t))$ satisfies the adic coefficient datum. Open slice localization identifies $(A_n)_X|_U=(A_n)_U$ with the constant-section normalization. Restriction preserves limits, so it also identifies $B_X|_U=B_U$, respecting every quotient projection; likewise for $j'$.

source.place: Tags 099L, 09BN; properties.tex Tags 01OW, 01OY; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6. Elementary ideal and two-term-resolution checks for the specified DVR.

proof.text: Write $C_W(H)=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W)$ and $\eta_H:H\to C_W(H)$ for its quotient augmentation. The constant/completed coefficient equivalence identifies this functor and its unit with Koszul completion. The ringed Koszul reflector makes $C_W(H)$ intrinsically complete and says that $\eta_H$ is invertible exactly for intrinsically complete $H$. This also identifies the completeness convention in the item: an object satisfying the Roos-triangle definition is isomorphic to $C_W(H)$, because both are fibers of its same product-shift map; it is therefore intrinsically complete and its actual unit is invertible. Conversely the invertible actual unit supplies the defining Roos triangle. Hence the two notions of completeness agree here; this argument does not identify an arbitrary map to a triangle fiber with the completion unit.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion); algebraization.tex Tags 099B and 0A0E; compare Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24.

proof.text: For $e=j$ or $j'$, restriction $e^*$ is exact and preserves countable products, and these products are exact on both pro-etale module categories. Apply the exact-product/strict-limit comparison to $F=e^*$. Derived tensor-pullback identifies $e^*(H\otimes^L(A_n))$ with $(e^*H)\otimes^L(A_n)$; it uses precisely the quotient-compatible coefficient identifications of Step 1. We obtain $e^*C(H)\cong C(e^*H)$. The augmentation clause of the strict-limit comparison carries $e^*\eta_H$ to $\eta_{e^*H}$, as actual maps. Therefore restriction preserves completeness. The definition of completed pullback is ordinary pullback followed by this completion, with ordinary-to-completed comparison $\eta$; along the open, ordinary pullback is the exact restriction. Consequently $Le^*_{\mathrm{comp}}\cong e^*$ on complete objects, with the comparison equal to its invertible completion unit.

source.place: Tags 099N(2),(5), 09BN; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4. Canonical strict-limit comparison, including its augmentation clause.

proof.text: By the ambient open-normalization theorem, the derived open-extension unit $u_K:K\to e^*e_!K$ is the identity under the specified slice identification, and $e_!$ is fully faithful on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The completed-extension theorem applies with the adic datum verified in Step 1 and makes $e_!K$ complete whenever $K$ is complete (apply it to the identity base-change square for $e$). Together with Step 3 this restricts the adjunction to complete objects, without altering its unit. These subcategories are full, so the same Hom bijection proves full faithfulness on them. This establishes all of clause (1).

source.place: Tag 09BN (lemma-open-immersion); sites-modules.tex Tag 0F6Z; completed-extension comparison, preservation clause.

proof.text:
Apply the ambient open base-change normalization to the identity scheme map $X\to X$ equipped with the coefficient map $B_X\to(A_n)_X$, and its restricted map over $U$. It gives an $(A_n)_X$-linear isomorphism
$$r_n:(j_!K)\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^{A_n}(K\otimes^L_{B_U}(A_n)_U).$$
Its inverse is exactly the open-unit transpose specified there. For the ring diagram $(B_W\to(A_n)_W)_n$, the strict-coefficient-system clause of that same normalization gives these maps simultaneously, including every quotient transition. Reading an $A_n$-module as a $B$-module commutes with open extension: its extension presheaf has the same summands with the action restricted, and module sheafification gives the same underlying sheaf. Thus $r_\bullet$ is the reduction-tower comparison needed below, not a choice of unrelated levelwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI, 0E8I; normalization on ringed coefficient diagrams.

proof.text: Let $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_U}(A_n)_U$. Exactness of $j_!$ gives $\mathcal H^q(j_!K_n)=j_!\mathcal H^q(K_n)$ and preserves every cohomological interval. For each constructible cohomology sheaf, take its defining finite partition of $U$. Viewed in $X$, these are still locally closed constructible pieces: $U$ is a constructible open in the Noetherian $X$. Add the reduced closed complement $Z=X\setminus U$, whose scheme structure exists by the closed-subset lemma. The ringed open-closed theorem gives the original restriction on $U$ and zero restriction on $Z$. Thus the same finite local constant modules, together with zero on $Z$, witness constructibility of $j_!\mathcal H^q(K_n)$. By Step 5 the reductions of $j_!K$ are precisely these objects, all in the same interval as the reductions of $K$; completeness is Step 4. The definition of the integral category now gives $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$. Also $j^*P\in D^b_c(U,R)$: intersect each finite reduction's partition with $U$, and use exact restriction, Step 3, and the restriction/reduction comparison. No finite-Tor assumption has entered.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(2),(3), p. 50; the direct finite-partition argument uses the actual definition in this DAG. Stacks Tags 03DJ, 09BN, 09AG.

proof.text:
Put $H=j_!K\otimes^L_{B_X}P$ and $H_U=K\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*P$. The ambient open tensor isomorphism $\gamma^B:H\to j_!H_U$ is the inverse open-unit transpose, not an arbitrary isomorphism. Its reductions, read through Step 5 and the derived tensor-pullback comparison for $B\to A_n$, are the finite open tensor isomorphisms
$$\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet=((j_!K)_n\otimes^L_{A_n}P_n)_n\longrightarrow j_!S_\bullet,\qquad S_\bullet=(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}j^*P_n)_n.$$
Here these are strict derived-system maps by the coefficient-diagram clause of the open-normalization theorem. Their quotient-augmentation square with $\gamma^B$ commutes before taking limits. Indeed the inverse comparisons are characterized by transposition of $u_K\otimes1$; restriction of the quotient map commutes with $u_K$ by naturality. Under tensor balancing both orders send $(x\otimes y)\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. This is the same section map after any coefficient transition, with unchanged tensor degrees and signs, so the equality is in the system models and descends there. This proves the required augmentation square rather than testing equality by derived evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, with sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I and the specified open-unit transpose; apply the ringed-diagram normalization to the quotient diagram.

proof.text:
The derived extension/limit theorem supplies product preservation for $j_!$. With its exactness and exact countable products, the strict-limit comparison supplies its specified natural isomorphism $\lambda_j:j_!R\lim S_\bullet\to R\lim j_!S_\bullet$, including compatibility with strict augmentations. In the integral operation formulas, $R\lim T_\bullet=j_!K\widehat\otimes^L_RP$ and $R\lim S_\bullet=K\widehat\otimes^L_Rj^*P$. Realize the integral open projection datum used in def-exchange-projection by its canonical strict-reduction construction
$$\gamma^c=\lambda_j^{-1}\circ R\lim(\gamma_\bullet).$$
The functorial derived limit sends the strict-system isomorphism to an isomorphism. Applying it to the augmentation square of Step 7, and then using the augmentation clause for $\lambda_j$, gives the equality of actual maps
$$\gamma^c\chi_{j_!K,P}=j_!(\chi_{K,j^*P})\gamma^B.$$
The maps denoted $\chi$ here are exactly the quotient-augmentation maps in the tensor-completion theorem. This constructs and normalizes the supplied open datum; the definition of exchange/projection alone is not being used as a preservation or coherence theorem.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, p. 22; Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8, pp. 49–50; Stacks Tags 099M and 09BP, and the augmentation-normalized strict-limit comparison.

proof.text: Step 6 puts $(j_!K,P)$ and $(K,j^*P)$ in the respective bounded constructible integral categories. The tensor-completion theorem applies since $X,U$ are qcqs and $\ell$ is invertible; it makes both displayed $\chi$ maps isomorphisms. Thus the equation of Step 8 also expresses $\gamma^c$ as $j_!\chi\circ\gamma^B\circ\chi^{-1}$. Restrict it to $U$. Step 3 identifies restriction of the quotient-augmentation completion map with the quotient-augmentation map of the restricted ordinary tensor. The ambient tensor normalization identifies $j^*\gamma^B$ with the identity. Hence the restricted equation is $(j^*\gamma^c)\chi=\chi$ under exactly the open-unit and tensor identifications, so cancellation of the invertible $\chi$ gives $j^*\gamma^c=1$. Both the identity and invertibility assertions concern this constructed completed map.

source.place: Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8, pp. 49–50; Stacks 0GL1. Cancellation after the actual completion-unit equation of Step 8.

proof.text:
Apply the completed extension-zero comparison with $g=h$, $g_U=a$ and the datum checked in Step 1. It gives the required isomorphism $\beta^c$. More explicitly, retain the reduction comparison of Step 5 and let $\beta_\bullet$ be the strict family of finite open base-change maps. Finite open-exchange/scalar compatibility supplies this family and its inverse compatibly with every $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ and with the inverse-unit transposes. The canonical map in the cited completed-extension statement is therefore exactly
$$\beta^c=\lambda_{j'}^{-1}\circ R\lim(\beta_\bullet):Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\longrightarrow j'_!La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K,$$
where $\lambda_{j'}$ is the same specified strict-limit comparison as in Step 8. Its endpoint completeness and invertibility are part of the cited theorem, and no alternative comparison selected from its endpoints is used.

source.place: Tags 099N(5) and 09BN; strict finite-map/augmentation normalization of the cited completed extension-zero comparison.

proof.text: Finally restrict the last formula along $j'$. The exact-product/strict-limit comparison of Step 3 passes this restriction through $R\lim$, with its actual augmentation. The inverse-unit formula for $\beta$ in the open-normalization theorem gives $j'^*\beta_\bullet=1$ after the finite pullback-composition and open-unit identifications; its coefficient-diagram clause gives this equation for the strict systems themselves. The pullback-composition maps here use only the finite constant rings, so their coefficient inverse-image identifications satisfy the hypotheses of the derived pullback-composition lemma. Taking their derived limit gives the canonical comparison $j'^*Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\cong La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$. Under it, $R\lim(j'^*\beta_\bullet)$ is the identity. Restriction of $\lambda_{j'}$ becomes the identity limit comparison under $j'^*j'_!=1$: its product comparison is identity on each projection and its normalized Roos comparison uses that same product map on both summands. The augmentation clause identifies its units as well. Consequently $j'^*\beta^c=1$ under the stated canonical identifications. This is a functor applied to an equality of strict-system maps, not an assumption that finite reductions detect equality of completed morphisms.

source.place: Tags 09BN and 099N(5); sites-modules.tex Tag 0F6Z; strict-system inverse-unit normalization and augmentation-normalized limit comparison.

title: Completed open restriction, constructibility and normalization of the open maps
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum and coefficients $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U'&\xrightarrow{a}&U\\ j'\downarrow&&\downarrow j\\ X'&\xrightarrow{h}&X\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of finite-type $k$-schemes with $j$ open [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. On each small pro-etale site use $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the ordinary module derived category $D(B_W)$, and its full derived-complete constructible category $D^b_c(W,R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Use exact termwise ringed-slice extension by zero and restriction, $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Then:

(1) Open restriction preserves derived completeness and canonically equals completed open pullback, with the comparison from ordinary restriction equal to the completion unit. Its unit $K\to j^*j_!K$ is the identity under the open-slice identification. The derived open extension is fully faithful on the complete subcategories.

(2) For every $K\in D^b_c(U,R)$, without a finite-Tor hypothesis, $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and
$$(j_!K)\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X\cong j_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_{B_U}(A_n)_U\bigr).$$
These canonical comparisons commute with the strict quotient transitions. Extension by zero preserves the cohomological interval of every finite reduction.

(3) For $K\in D^b_c(U,R)$ and $P\in D^b_c(X,R)$, let $\gamma^B:j_!K\otimes^L_{B_X}P\to j_!(K\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*P)$ be the canonical ambient open tensor map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Under the canonical completion maps $\chi$ of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], the completed open projection map $\gamma^c$ of [def-exchange-projection] satisfies
$$\gamma^c\chi_{j_!K,P}=j_!(\chi_{K,j^*P})\gamma^B.$$
The map $\gamma^c$ is an isomorphism and $j^*\gamma^c$ is the identity under the specified open tensor identifications. For $\beta^c:Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\to j'_!La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$, use exactly the strict-reduction construction of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]; the map $\beta^c$ is an isomorphism and its restriction $j'^*\beta^c$ is the identity under the canonical pullback-composition and open-unit identifications. These assertions concern the actual completed morphisms and their units, with the quotient transitions retained.
